title: Readiness for the first macrostep
statement: Let $W$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $T\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that for every Boolean input $y$, $W$ halts after exactly $b(T(|y|)+1)$ steps and outputs the little-endian binary expansion of $T(|y|)$, and suppose that $n\le T(n)$ for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$. For every Boolean input $x$, there is a time $t$ at which the schedule machine, started on the tagged encoding of $x$, is in the macrostep-check state, its unary-counter head is at position $1$, its guide head is at position $0$, its unary-counter tape has $(a+1)(T(|x|)+1)$ markers, and its guide tape has radius $3(a+1)(T(|x|)+1)$.
hypotheses_covered: W is a finite machine over Booleans
a and b are natural numbers
For every Boolean input y, W halts and outputs the binary digits of T(|y|) after exactly b(T(|y|)+1) steps
n ≤ T(n) for every natural n
replaced:
Let $W$ compute on every input $x$ the binary expansion of $T(|x|)$ within
$b\,(T(|x|)+1)$ steps, and suppose $n \le T(n)$ for all $n$.  Then for every
word $x$ there is a time $t$ at which the schedule controller built from $W$ and
$a$, run on the embedded input, is in the counter-test phase with unary head at
$1$, guide head at the origin, unary counter tape with $(a+1)(T(|x|)+1)$
markers, and guide tape of radius $3(a+1)(T(|x|)+1)$.
